questions.question: Which smart pointer represents exclusive ownership?
questions.explanation: std::unique_ptr owns an object exclusively and releases it when the pointer is destroyed.

questions.question: std::shared_ptr uses reference counting to manage shared ownership.
questions.explanation: A shared object remains alive while at least one std::shared_ptr owns it.

questions.question: A non-owning observer for an object managed by std::shared_ptr is called ____.
questions.explanation: std::weak_ptr can observe a shared object without increasing its reference count.

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: std::make_unique<int>(42) creates an int initialized to 42, and dereferencing the pointer prints that value.
